calls.reason: The statement is hedged with “seem.” Tom’s Guide links the March 2 outage to demand, while the March 27 postmortem identifies networking problems; these support some capacity pressure without settling the broader wording.
The April 15 incident confirms an outage, and Anthropic disclosed $30 billion in financing. Neither establishes what dependable service would cost or whether Anthropic could afford it.

Anthropic’s SEC filing reports subscriptions at just 17% of revenue in 2025 and 20% in the first half of 2026. That strongly undermines the broad claim that subscriptions supplied most revenue at each named company, regardless of subsidy levels.

NVIDIA’s inventory disclosure does not identify sold GPUs awaiting installation. TechRadar’s later AWS reporting supports some warehousing, but neither source establishes years’ worth of stored GPUs at the time of the claim.

GitHub adopted usage billing in June, but Anthropic expanded allowances and October reporting found substantial subscription discounts. The evidence is mixed, actual delivery costs are missing, and the forecast has no firm deadline.

Anthropic’s May capacity announcement links added compute to higher usage limits. It does not establish a forced reliability requirement or show that stable service requires halting enrollment or massively increasing inference spending.
